Obros, the Thunderous One, is a mythical deity associated with the Ob River, one of the longest rivers in Russia. He is revered as a powerful and awe-inspiring figure, often depicted with a mighty staff in hand and surrounded by thunder and lightning.

As the god of the Ob River, Obros is believed to be the embodiment of the river's raw power and force, which is evident in its roaring rapids, turbulent currents, and thundering waterfalls. He is revered as a symbol of nature's might and unpredictability, commanding respect and reverence from those who venture upon the river's waters.

Obros is associated with the dramatic landscapes and natural phenomena along the Ob River, including the taiga forests, tundra, and rugged mountains that the river traverses. He is believed to be the guardian of these pristine wilderness areas, protecting them from harm and ensuring their continued existence for future generations to appreciate and cherish.

As the Thunderous One, Obros is also associated with the thunderstorms that often accompany the river's powerful currents. He is believed to wield the thunder and lightning as symbols of his authority, and his booming voice is said to echo through the valleys and canyons along the river, commanding both awe and reverence.

Obros is honored as a deity of great power and majesty, a force of nature to be respected and feared, and a symbol of the untamed wilderness and natural beauty of the Ob River. He serves as a reminder of the awe-inspiring power of nature and the need to respect and protect our rivers and their surrounding environments for the benefit of all living beings.
